about: Eval C — ranking quality of the data layer (DESIGN.md §10.1 C). No LLM involved.
Golden cases encode DOMAIN TRUTH about where scenes are, not whatever the current
scoring happens to return. That is the point: a dataset written from current output
can only detect change, never tell you the ranking is wrong.
Relevance gains: 3 = the defining scene for the genre, 2 = a major scene,
1 = notable. Gains feed NDCG; Recall@k only cares about membership.
Cases with "known_gap" are expected to fail: they document a real shortcoming in
the seed data or the scoring, each with the fix. They are measured and reported but
do not gate CI — so the gap stays visible instead of being quietly dropped, and the
runner shouts if one starts passing.
Ranking is tie-tolerant: positions use competition ranking (equal scores share a
rank), because the tie-break within a score is alphabetical and arbitrary — failing
on it would measure name order, not scene quality.
v2 (roadmap 1.10): reseeded from 500 artists/genre with tag verification. Three gaps
closed, one narrowed, and one new gap recorded — formula v1 counts bands, so it
measures VOLUME, and any golden case that really asserts INFLUENCE will fail until
the scoring gains an influence signal (DECISIONS.md D1 deferred refinements).
v3 (roadmap 1.11): D1a amendment — solo artists count, and signals are never
discarded, only re-attached. Coverage went from 485 signals to 2,070. Both
remaining gaps now share one cause: volume vs influence (roadmap 1.12).

cases.source: spike S3 metro_ranking: Bay Area 21 bands, Greater LA 14
cases.rationale: Bay Area thrash is the textbook case — Metallica, Exodus, Testament, Death Angel, Ruthie's Inn.

cases.source: spike S3 city_ranking: LA 13, SF 9, Chicago 9
cases.rationale: No must_rank_first and k=5, both deliberately: at city level the Bay Area scene is split across SF, Oakland and Richmond, so LA leads legitimately, and Chicago (9 bands in the spike too) sits in the same cluster. The defensible claim is that all three are top-5 thrash cities, not that they hold exact positions.

cases.source: spike S3 city_ranking: Seattle 23 bands, +53% over #2
cases.rationale: If Seattle is ever not #1 for grunge, the scoring is broken.

cases.source: spike S3 metro_ranking had Seattle #1 at 23 bands
cases.rationale: Closed in 1.10 by seeding the Greater Seattle metro (Seattle–Tacoma–Bellevue MSA). Before that, Seattle parented straight to Washington and this query returned Greater Los Angeles.

cases.source: spike S3 city_ranking: Helsinki 9, Gothenburg 7, Stockholm 6
cases.rationale: The Gothenburg sound defines melodeath, but Finland out-produces it by volume — so the claim is top-3, not first.
Both must be top-3. Which of the two leads is a volume-vs-influence question — see melodic-death-metal-country-sweden-first.
Birthplace of the genre; LA is the other undisputed major scene.

cases.source: domain truth: Atlanta is a defining hip hop scene (OutKast, Goodie Mob, and the whole trap lineage)
cases.rationale: Closed in 1.10 by fetching 500 artists per genre instead of 200 — Atlanta now ranks 3rd. It previously had no location row at all.

cases.known_gap: Sweden ranks 3rd (88.4) behind Finland (100) and Germany (91.3). With 1.11's complete attribution the three are within 12 points of each other, but Sweden's claim to melodeath is that Gothenburg INVENTED it — At the Gates, In Flames, Dark Tranquillity — which is influence, not volume. Formula v1 counts artists, so it cannot express this at any level of coverage.
cases.fix: Needs an influence signal (roadmap 1.12): historic-era multiplier, popularity, or tag-vote strength. Coverage is no longer the confound — 1.11 fixed that — so this is now purely a weighting question.
cases.source: domain truth: the Gothenburg sound is the origin of melodic death metal

cases.known_gap: Recall is now perfect — after 1.11's D1a amendment all three of Detroit, Berlin and London are top-3, and Detroit's scene finally contains Juan Atkins, Derrick May, Jeff Mills and Carl Craig instead of being empty of its own founders. Only `must_rank_first` still fails: London leads on volume (100 vs Berlin 58.3, Detroit 54.2), because it genuinely has more techno-tagged artists than the city that invented the genre.
cases.fix: Same question as melodic-death-metal-country-sweden-first, and the same answer: an influence signal (roadmap 1.12). Both remaining gaps are now one decision — whether scoring stays pure volume — rather than two data problems.
cases.source: domain truth: Detroit is the origin of techno; Berlin is its second home
